turn1.message: I have 30 minutes, solo, no Crucible and no dungeons. What should I do?
turn1.draft:
Great — with 30 minutes, solo, and no Crucible or dungeons, do this:

Primary (best fit): Complete the active Edge of Fate quest step — “Kepler Uplink”
- Why: It’s an active campaign quest for your Titan and is a single mission objective (usually fits well inside 30 minutes).  
- What to do: Open Quests → Edge of Fate → Launch the Kepler Uplink mission and finish the objective(s). Accept whatever rewards and next-step quest appears.

Backup (if you want repeatable play/fast runs): Run Haunted Altars of Sorrow
- Why: It’s available to your account and your Triumph “Waves of Altars of Sorrow” is at 92% — a couple of short runs may finish it.  
- What to do: Launch Haunted Altars of Sorrow from Activities → play through the wave rounds; focus on clearing waves quickly and finishing the activity.

Which do you want to run now — the Kepler Uplink mission or Haunted Altars?

turn2.draft:
Best loot in your constraints: Haunted Altars of Sorrow (solo, ~30 min runs).

Why: it’s a seasonal, repeatable activity available to your Titan from the candidates list and can drop activity-specific rewards and engrams more often than the record/triumph cleanup. A couple quick runs in 30 minutes gives more direct loot chance than just repeating story missions.

What to do (maximize loot in one 30‑minute session)
- Launch Haunted Altars of Sorrow from Activities → Seasonal or Patrol selections.  
- Prioritize completing the activity and any in-activity bonus objectives (they often grant extra drops).  
- Kill wave leaders and finish rounds quickly to trigger completion rewards; collect any chests/loot that spawn during waves.  
- Pick up all engrams and check Postmaster/character slots between runs.  
- If you have any related bounties or weekly tasks (on that character) that overlap the activity, do those while you play to multiply rewards.

Backup (if you want Triumph progress + loot): keep running Haunted Altars until your “Waves of Altars of Sorrow” Triumph hits 100% — you’re at 92% so a couple runs may finish it and grant whatever Triumph reward exists while still giving loot.

Want me to check your current build/loadout to suggest a faster, loot‑focused setup for the Titan before you launch?

build.message: Look at my current Titan build. What's the single biggest improvement I could make?
drafts:
Swap your equipped Energy SMG (Calus Mini-Tool) for an Energy hand cannon (or another mid/long‑range precision energy weapon). 

Why: your Rose (Kinetic hand cannon) already runs Opening Shot + Rampage—pairing it with an energy hand cannon gives consistent precision damage at longer ranges, makes it easier to secure the single- and multi‑kills that keep Rampage active, and reduces awkward range overlaps that force you into melee when you’d rather keep using Rose. It’s a single, verifiable equipment change and keeps your equipped Exotic (Synthoceps) in place.

How to do it:
- Open your inventory on your Titan.
- Move the Calus Mini‑Tool out of the Energy slot (vault or unequip).
- Equip an owned Energy hand cannon (or pull one from the vault) into the Energy slot.
- Test in a Vanguard or playlist activity and swap if the range/feel isn’t right.

Backup (if you don’t own a suitable energy hand cannon): equip a kinetic/energy pairing that increases precision consistency — e.g., a longer‑range SMG or adaptive scout — so your Rose’s Rampage uptime isn’t frequently interrupted by bad range matchups.

- Unequip or move Calus Mini‑Tool out of the Energy slot.

If you don’t own a suitable Energy hand cannon, the single next-best swap is to equip an energy weapon with better precision/range than the SMG (for the same reason).
